tldr: CodeRL is a framework that applies actor-critic deep reinforcement learning to pretrained language models for program synthesis, using unit test signals as dense feedback to improve both training and generation, achieving new state-of-the-art results on APPS and MBPP benchmarks.
contributions: Proposing CodeRL, an actor-critic RL framework that formulates program synthesis as an RL problem to optimize pretrained LMs using unit test signals
Introducing a critic model trained as an error predictor to provide dense token-level feedback signals during training
Designing a novel inference-time generation procedure with critical sampling that uses example unit tests and critic scores to regenerate and repair programs
Extending CodeT5 with enhanced pretraining objectives (including NTP), larger model sizes, and 10x larger pretraining data (GCPY, 10.5B tokens)
Achieving new SOTA on APPS and zero-shot SOTA on MBPP, releasing improved CodeT5-large (770M)
methods: The authors formulate program synthesis as an RL problem where the pretrained LM acts as an actor policy that samples synthetic programs, and a critic model predicts functional correctness (CompileError, RuntimeError, FailedTest, PassedTest). The critic is trained to minimize cross-entropy loss on unit test outcomes and provides token-level value estimates via max-pooled hidden states. Training uses REINFORCE with a greedy decoding baseline and critic-weighted intermediate returns to reduce gradient variance. During inference, a critical sampling strategy regenerates programs for candidates passing example unit tests, and repairs failed programs using compiler error information concatenated with top critic-ranked candidates.
results: CodeRL achieves new SOTA on the APPS benchmark with more than 2% pass@1, 6% pass@5, and 20% pass@1000. It sets a new zero-shot SOTA on MBPP with 63.0% pass@80, surpassing a finetuned GPT-137B's 61.4%. The RL method is model-agnostic and produces consistent gains across various large-scale models. The released CodeT5-large (770M) outperforms many pretrained LMs of much larger sizes.
limitations: Existing models trained with next-token prediction in a teacher-forcing manner accumulate errors during test time when conditioning on previously sampled tokens rather than ground-truth tokens, an issue that worsens for complex competition-level problems. Token-matching scores like BLEU poorly correlate with functional correctness of complete programs, making evaluation non-trivial. Prior RL-based and execution-guided synthesis approaches were limited to domain-specific programming languages, whereas this work targets general-purpose languages like Python with natural language problem specifications.
